corrected_fields.summary: The OECD Global Debt Report 2026 is the third edition of an annual publication analyzing global sovereign and corporate bond market trends from 2007 to 2026. Chapter 1 examines sovereign borrowing requirements, funding strategies, debt-to-GDP dynamics, borrowing costs, yield curve shapes, refinancing risks, and market liquidity for OECD countries. Chapter 2 covers corporate debt markets (bonds, syndicated loans, private credit) focusing on credit spread drivers, AI expansion impact, and whether corporate debt has become more equity-like. Chapter 3 analyzes the investor base evolution for government and corporate bonds.
corrected_fields.why_it_matters: This annual report provides authoritative, comprehensive data on global debt market structure, investor base composition, and market liquidity conditions. Market participants need this information to understand sovereign and corporate debt market resilience, refinancing risks, and potential vulnerabilities under stress conditions. The investor base analysis is particularly relevant for understanding who holds sovereign debt and how ownership composition affects market dynamics.
corrected_fields.macro_context: The report addresses key macro-financial linkages including sovereign debt-to-GDP dynamics across OECD countries, refinancing risks at elevated debt levels, corporate credit spread drivers, and implications of AI expansion on corporate debt markets. It provides the analytical foundation for assessing global debt market sustainability.
corrected_fields.market_structure_context: Chapter 1 includes analysis of market liquidity in government bond secondary markets; Chapter 3 provides detailed investor base analysis for both sovereign and corporate bonds including changes in holdings at aggregate and regional levels from 2007-2026; report draws on dedicated liquidity surveys
